question.leadin: Answer these questions about Spanish conquistadores.
question.text: Pizarro defeated this last Inca emperor, who was ransomed for a room filled with gold before being executed anyway.
question.clue: He offered to fill a large room with gold and silver for his ransom, but the Spaniards didn't release him.

swap.text: The Incan empire was centered in this modern day country, whose capital is Lima.
swap.clue: The founder of a civilization based in this country put his capital where a golden staff sank into the ground.

question.text: Alongside Bernardo O'Higgins, de San Martin fought for the independence of this future nation. The Battle of Junin was part of this country's war of independence.
question.clue: A culture from this country based in Sipan was known for pottery depicting exaggerated sexual acts, and another civilization in this country was known for geoglyphs depicting Condors and Herons.

swap.text: Identify the Spaniard who conquered the Incan Empire.
swap.clue: This man received help from longtime partner Diego Almagro, but he was killed by Almagro's forces in the Battle of Las Salinas.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain precious metal in pre-Columbian South America.
question.text: Tales of gold in South America inspired legends of this fictitious "City of Gold." This fictional place was sought by Europeans like Walter Raleigh and Gonzalo de Quesada.
question.answerHtml: El Dorado [accept Manoa; do NOT accept or prompt on “Cibola”]
question.clue: During the first part of the journey in which Orellana travelled the length of the Amazon, a valley of Cinnamon and this place were the targets of Gonzalo Pizzaro.

swap.text: This founder of the city of Lima who conquered the Inca Empire held Atahualpa prisoner in a room full of gold before executing him.
swap.clue: Gonzalo also led a revolt against Blasco Nunez Vela for attempting to enforce the New Laws under Charles V. Another man with this surname served under Balboa and briefly served as mayor of Panama City.

question.text: The mita was used by Spanish rulers to obtain a labor force for this largest silver mine in the Spanish Empire, in which thousands died from mercury poisoning. It lies in present-day Bolivia.
question.clue: Economic production in this city took off following the remote discovery of Huancavelica, which supplied material crucial for a process invented by Bartolome de Medina widely used in this city.

swap.text: After sacking Ankara in Turkey, Tamerlane allegedly made a pyramid of these objects.
swap.clue: Timur allegedly built pyramids out of these body parts, the protective structure for the brain, which would terrify his enemies.

question.leadin: The execution of Antonio de Arriaga instigated a rebellion led by a man with this regnal name.
question.text: Give this two-word name of an indigenous Peruvian rebel leader who claimed descent from the final Sapa Inca. That Neo-Incan ruler with this regnal name was executed by the Spanish in 1572.
question.clue: The legitimate son of Manco Capac, he was captured an executed for the death of Friar Diego Ortiz.

swap.text: Machu Picchu was a major city of this Peruvian civilization that was conquered by Francisco Pizarro.
swap.clue: One ruler of these people allegedly gained a fortune from places termed the "Outer Belt" and the "Fire Belt," and another earned a name meaning "overturner of the world" or "earthshaker" after stones supposedly came to life to help him repel Chanka invaders.

question.leadin: One hypothesis suggests that this culture may have created early hot air balloons to view certain artistic features.
question.text: Name this Peruvian culture that succeeded the Paracas culture. These people carved stone geoglyphs, such as monkeys and spiders, into the desert in their namesake "lines."
question.clue: Paul Kosok and Maria Reiche (RAI-keh) mapped structures created by these people.

swap.leadin: Jim Woodmann constructed a balloon using primitive materials in order to show the plausibility of the "balloon theory" regarding these things.
swap.text: Identify these archaeological features which include the Condor and the Hummingbird. Jainer Jesus Flores Vigo was arrested for using a truck as an "attack against cultural heritage" on these things in 2018.
swap.answerHtml: Nazca Lines [or Nasca Lines; or Andes Lines; or Nazca Drawings]
swap.clue: These things were damaged by Greenpeace activists wearing improper footwear as part of a 2014 protest.

question.leadin: According to their own legends, these people originated in the village of Pagari-tampu, and they referred to the world they knew as Tahuantinsuyu.
question.text: Identify this pre-Columbian civilization which in 1471 conquered the kingdom of Chimor. They worship the creator god Viracocha, and had a cultural center at Macchu Picchu.
question.clue: Descendants of this empire's royalty included Garcilaso de la Vega, and this empire was sometimes named for the four administrative suyus that it was divided into.

swap.text: This emperor of the Inca wrote special hymns for the Situa Festival. This man, whose name means "Earthshaker," pacified the Chanca peoples and his son, Tupo Inca, built the Saqsaywaman Fort in Cusco.
swap.clue: This ruler, who legendarily subjugated the (+) Chanka people with stone warriors, organized his realm into four suyus.

question.text: The Acari Valley had previously been ruled by these people, some of whose puquios aqueducts are still used today.
question.clue: This culture built the Cantalloc ("cahn-TAH-yoke")Aqueducts, exemplifying the corkscrew entrances of their puquios ("poo-KEE-ohʼs").

swap.leadin: After being attacked by the rival Chanka people, this ruler is said to have called on the sun god Inti to turn stones into pururauca warriors to defend his city.
swap.text: Name this son of Viracocha who transformed the Kingdom of Cuzco into the Incan Empire in the 15th century.
swap.clue: This king commissioned life-sized gold statues of animals and plant for the central garden of his Coricancha temple.

question.leadin: Father Jose Domingo Duquesne ("dew-CANE") was tasked with studying these people's namesake language, which was also called Chibcha.
question.text: Name these people governed in the north by zaques ("SAH-kays") and in the south by zipas ("SEE-pahs") until conquistadors invaded their "confederation."
question.clue: This people, who mined salt in large gacha pots and imported gold for tunjo figures of humans or animals at Guatavita.

swap.leadin: The artwork of this culture shows a spider god called the "Decapitator" holding a knife and a severed head, an indication that these people practiced human sacrifice.
swap.text: Name this civilization whose adobe temple at Huaca del Sol near Cerro Blanco is considered by many to be the largest pre-Columbian structure in South America.

question.leadin: This civilization had its capital at Chanchan, to the north of Trujillo, and its language of Quingnam has been called the "Fisherman's language."
question.text: Name this South American civilization that arose around 900 AD, and was known for its pottery and metallurgy.
question.clue: These people succeeded the Moche, and they ruled from their capital at Chan Chan.

swap.text: Peruvian magnates on these islands hired blackbirders to kidnap workers to mine guano. Spain seized these islands to acquire those mines in the 1860s, but was repulsed by a coalition of South American countries.
swap.clue: Kidnapped Chinese workers were also kept in slave-like conditions on these Peruvian islands in order to harvest guano. Spain seized these islands in 1864, which prompted a war in which Chile and Peru fought to take them back.
